title: A Salt for the Sigil Again
premise: Gideon Villalobos has spent thirty years keeping the Thornfell gate sealed, pretending the old gods behind it are dead. But when prayers start being answered—crops blooming overnight, the sick healed at terrible prices—it becomes clear something has slipped through and is wearing the young King Aldric like a glove. Hunted by royal wardens who cannot see the corruption they serve, Gideon gathers a found family of outcasts: a disgraced priestess, a smuggler who owes them a life debt, and the king's runaway sister. To free Aldric, they must reach the gate on the thirteenth moon and perform an unbinding that will cost Gideon their memories of everyone they love; in the end, Gideon pays it, the god is starved back behind the seal, and the family chooses to find them again, name by name.
about_author: Jonah Zhou is a former trail-crew cook in the northern ranges who writes fantasy about people who live just outside the maps. Their short fiction has appeared in several small magazines, and this is their second novel.

chapters.title: The Gate That Answers
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A dying shepherd prays at the sealed gate and his fever breaks by morning—but his shadow walks off without him. Gideon inspects the seal and finds one sigil freshly warm. Emotional beat: dread beneath routine, the first crack in thirty years of quiet.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Tithe
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. On the mountain roads, Gideon catches Ryn Sable, a smuggler who once saved their life, moving cargo that whispers. Ryn swears she was paid in answered prayers, not coin. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; old debts resurfacing.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Want
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Royal wardens arrive hunting 'heretics' whose prayers were answered, burning a village that worshipped nothing. Gideon realizes the crown isn't suppressing the old gods—it's feeding them. Emotional beat: cold fury, the law revealed as predator.

chapters.title: The Sister in the Snow
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV (the king's runaway sister). Fleeing the palace after her brother stopped recognizing her, Isolde crosses Thornfell and stumbles into Gideon's watchpost. She carries a letter in Aldric's handwriting that he doesn't remember writing. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Deciphering the letter with Maerin, a defrocked priestess hiding in the valley, they learn the unbinding rite must be completed before the thirteenth new moon—or the thing wearing Aldric becomes permanent. Emotional beat: the clock starts; fear becomes resolve.

chapters.title: Prayers Priced in Bone
chapters.summary: Maerin's POV. The team visits a valley where every miracle has left a hollowed-out worshipper. Maerin recognizes the liturgy—the god is using rites she once served. Emotional beat: guilt, and the first taste of what they're truly fighting.

chapters.title: Ryn's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ryn's POV. Ryn leads them through smugglers' tunnels toward the capital, revealing she's been running messages for the crown under duress. Betrayal looms; instead she burns her ledger and joins fully. Emotional beat: choosing a side at personal ruin.

chapters.title: The City That Prays
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. In the capital, piety is mandatory and miracles are currency; the poor sell years of memory for healing. The team sees the god's economy up close. Emotional beat: horror at how easily corruption dresses as grace.

chapters.title: An Audience of One
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Using her name, Isolde gets close to Aldric—and finds him lucid for ninety seconds, begging her to cut the crown from his head before he forgets her again. Emotional beat: heartbreak; hope with a knife's edge.

chapters.title: Wardens at the Door
chapters.summary: Ryn's POV. The safehouse is raided. Maerin is captured; Gideon barely escapes with the rite's first component. Ryn covers their retreat and takes a warden's blade across the ribs. Emotional beat: cost made flesh; the family bleeds together.

chapters.title: The Priestess Interrogated
chapters.summary: Maerin's POV. In the cells, Maerin faces the High Warden—who is himself half-hollow, praying to the thing he serves. She learns the god's true name and its hunger's origin. Emotional beat: defiance under torture; knowledge won at pain.

chapters.title: Old Roads, Older Debts
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Retreating to Thornfell, Gideon reveals their history: they were the gate's last apprentice, and the previous keeper bound herself into the seal when the gods last woke. Emotional beat: vulnerability; the weight of inheritance.

chapters.title: A Bargain Below
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. To free Maerin, Isolde trades palace secrets to a warden captain who hates what the crown has become. The rescue succeeds but marks them all as traitors. Emotional beat: justice outside the law begins here.

chapters.title: The Second Sigil
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gathering the rite's components—a relic, a renunciation, a willing witness—they recover the keeper's iron bell from a flooded shrine. The god notices them for the first time and offers Gideon everything they've ever lost. Emotional beat: temptation sung sweetly.

chapters.title: What Gideon Wants
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Alone, Gideon nearly accepts the bargain: their dead mentor returned, their loneliness ended. Ryn interrupts without knowing why, and Gideon refuses. Emotional beat: the book's moral hinge—power refused in private.

chapters.title: Moon Twelve
chapters.summary: Maerin's POV. Freed and scarred, Maerin completes preparations but warns the unbinding requires a keeper to stand inside the seal—one turn of memories per sigil unbound. Three sigils. Emotional beat: quiet acceptance forming around an unspeakable price.

chapters.title: The Crown Comes Down
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. The team infiltrates the coronation renewal ceremony to take Aldric physically. It goes wrong; Ryn is captured covering the escape, and the king is taken deeper into the god's sanctum. Emotional beat: plan shattered, family scattered.

chapters.title: Hollow Victory
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. With one moon left, the god parades Ryn through the capital, offering her freedom if the others surrender. Instead the warden captain defects, bringing soldiers who've seen the hollowed poor. Emotional beat: the law finally bending toward justice.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. At the gate under the dark moon, Gideon enters the seal while Maerin chants and Isolde holds the bell. Sigil by sigil, Gideon surrenders their memories—mentor, roads, names. Climax: the god starves, screaming, as the seal closes on willing sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Empty Watchpost
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Aldric wakes whole and orders the prayer-economy dismantled, but Gideon stands blank-eyed at the gate, knowing no one. Isolde reads their own journal aloud to them. Emotional beat: grief and tenderness entwined.

chapters.title: Name by Name
chapters.summary: Ryn's POV. Recovering, Ryn begins reintroducing the family to Gideon—her debt repaid forward. Each retold memory returns a fragment, because love leaves traces the seal couldn't eat. Emotional beat: found family as literal restoration.

chapters.title: A Salt for the Sigil Again
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Months later, Gideon keeps the gate still—not alone now, with Maerin's rites, Isolde's letters, Ryn's roads, and a king who visits as a friend. They remember almost everything, and choose the work anyway. Final beat: power held lightly, guarded by the people who came back.
